title: hotfix: prevent SLO enforcer over-shedding that caused regional failover thrashing
author: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Emergency hotfix to address a regression in the SLO enforcer that allowed overly aggressive load-shedding. Under bursty traffic the enforcer would rapidly escalate shedding in a region, triggering regional failover. Failover events then caused traffic to concentrate in fallback regions which triggered shedding there and created a failover-thrashing loop. Root cause: A recent heuristic change (ENG-1789) adjusted the target shedding ratio based on short-window error/saturation signals but lacked two safety mechanisms: (1) a per-region shedding rate cap, and (2) a cooldown/backoff after a failover decision. The combination allowed the enforcer to increase shedding too fast and repeatedly trigger the regional failover circuit. Fix: Add conservative defaults and guardrails: - Cap per-region shedding ramp-up to 10% of capacity per 30s window (configurable). - Add per-region cooldown (default 2m) after a failover decision to avoid immediate re-evaluation. - Implement exponential backoff for repeated failover attempts with max backoff of 15m. - Introduce a lightweight regional circuit-breaker that prevents automated failover when downstream health is flapping. - Add detailed metrics and histograms (shed_rate, cooldown_remaining, backoff_count) and dashboard suggestions in ops docs. - Add unit and integration tests to reproduce the thrash scenario and validate cooldown/backoff behavior. Testing and rollout: Ran unit and integration tests locally and in CI. Integration test initially surfaced a timing race; adjusted wait intervals and made the test deterministic. We staged a canary rollout to us-west-2 for 30 minutes before full rollout. Observed stable shed rates and no failover re-triggers during canary. Notes: The change is conservative and designed to be safe-by-default for customer traffic. Operators can tune caps and cooldowns via the slo-enforcer config. See docs/ops/slo-enforcer.md for runtime knobs and recommended defaults.
